highlights.headline: Automatic updates
highlights.text: ClipLab checks for new versions and installs them by itself once nothing is rendering, then shows you what's new.

highlights.headline: Your call
highlights.text: In Settings > More, pick whether updates install by themselves, wait for your OK, or aren't checked at all. Check now and Update now are there too.

highlights.headline: Safe landings
highlights.text: Your settings and shorts are never touched, and if a new version doesn't start, ClipLab puts the old one back by itself.

highlights.headline: No more stray shutdowns
highlights.text: After a PC restart, starting ClipLab could close an unrelated program. It now checks it's really ClipLab first.

highlights.headline: Your game comes first
highlights.text: ClipLab now waits until you close your game before making shorts or installing updates, so your frames stay smooth mid-match. Clips line up and start rendering right after you're done. In a hurry? Hit Render now.

highlights.headline: Drag to trim
highlights.text: Grab the start or end of the re-cut timeline, or slide the whole window, and the player shows the exact frame you're cutting at. Works with a finger on your phone too.

highlights.headline: This pop-up!
highlights.text: Whenever ClipLab updates, you get a quick tour of what's new, confetti included.

highlights.headline: Patch history
highlights.text: Tap ✨ at the top of the app to look back at every update ClipLab has had.

highlights.headline: Request a feature
highlights.text: Got an idea? Write it up in the app and ClipLab opens a GitHub feature request with it filled in. Submit it there with a free GitHub account.

highlights.headline: Install ClipLab as an app
highlights.text: Put ClipLab on your taskbar or home screen so it opens like any other app.

highlights.headline: Subtitles are here
highlights.text: ClipLab writes what's said in your clip on screen, a few punchy words at a time, in Bold, Pop, Boxed or Clean, low, middle or up top. It all happens on your PC.

highlights.headline: Intro hook
highlights.text: Add a whoosh and a quick zoom punch to the first moment of every short, so people scrolling past stop on it.

highlights.headline: Ready to post
highlights.text: One button (or P) downloads your short and copies its caption, ready to paste into TikTok, YouTube Shorts or Reels.

highlights.headline: VALORANT joins the lab
highlights.text: VALORANT joins League and Siege. Any game works; the game setting just picks your hashtags.

highlights.headline: Your face, front and center
highlights.text: Pick your webcam in Settings > OBS and ClipLab puts it in a corner of OBS for you. Every short then gets a Webcam on top version: your reaction across the top, the play below.

highlights.headline: Run OBS from ClipLab
highlights.text: Choose your mic and which screen OBS records without digging through OBS's menus.

highlights.headline: Make it yours
highlights.text: Light or dark mode, plus five accent colors. Your phone matches automatically.

highlights.headline: Hear it save
highlights.text: Turn on a little chime, blip or pop for whenever your replay hotkey saves a clip.

highlights.headline: Longer shorts
highlights.text: Shorts can run up to 3 minutes, and the Getting started guide checks OBS keeps enough replay to fill them.

highlights.headline: Safe from sneaky websites
highlights.text: ClipLab now refuses requests other websites try to send it through your browser, so nothing can toss your clips or change your settings.

highlights.headline: Nothing for you to do
highlights.text: The app, your phone on home Wi-Fi and your own scripts keep working just like before.

title: Up and running in one line

highlights.headline: One-line installer
highlights.text: Paste one line into PowerShell and it sets up everything ClipLab needs, then opens the app. Run it again to update.

highlights.headline: Getting started guide
highlights.text: A checklist that reads OBS's settings, ticks off each step and finishes with a test replay.

title: Rainbow Six Siege joins the lab

highlights.headline: Rainbow Six Siege
highlights.text: Pick your game in Settings and captions get Siege hashtags.

highlights.headline: Shorts keep their game
highlights.text: Re-cuts and reels keep each short's own game, even after you switch.

highlights.headline: League auto-clipper
highlights.text: Saves a replay for you on multikills, aces, first blood and objective steals.

highlights.headline: Trimmed to the action
highlights.text: Each clip gets a tag file, so its short starts just before the first kill and ends right after the last.

highlights.headline: Replays to vertical shorts
highlights.text: Save a replay in OBS and about a minute later there's a 1080×1920 short with TRIPLE KILL-style text and a caption ready to paste.

highlights.headline: Two looks per clip
highlights.text: Blur fill shows the whole fight; Center crop fills the phone screen.

highlights.headline: The ClipLab app
highlights.text: Watch, keep, toss, re-cut and download your shorts, and stitch your best plays into highlight reels.

highlights.headline: One PC or two
highlights.text: Let a spare laptop do the rendering so your gaming PC doesn't have to.
